system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: New prompts are created by “best-shot prompting” from the programs database, and are then fed to the LLM to generate a new program.
system_prompt_style.note: Prompt assembled per iteration from sampled programs; no separate system prompt described.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: The input to FunSearch is a specification of the problem in the form of an evaluate function, an initial implementation of the function to evolve, which can be trivial, and potentially a skeleton.
env_context_strategy.note: Only the user-provided specification/skeleton; no repository exploration tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: the prompt is built as explained next
context_compaction.note: Each prompt is built fresh from k=2 sampled programs; no conversation history is accumulated.

observation_format.evidence_quote: evaluators score programs by executing them on inputs of interest and assessing the outputs using evaluate

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: a priority v2 function with no body is appended — the LLM will be in charge of completing the body of that function
tool_call_format.note: The model's output is code that is executed; no tool-call API.

tool_count.evidence_quote: The samples from the LLM (i.e., the generated programs) are sent to the evaluators, which score programs by executing them
tool_count.note: No tool schemas are exposed to the model; it emits code completions only.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: the LLM will be in charge of completing the body of that function
edit_primitive.note: The model rewrites the whole evolved function; closest value is whole_file_rewrite (function-level rewrite).

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: a user-provided program specification and skeleton
tool_schema_source.note: No tool schemas; the user-written specification/skeleton is the hand-authored interface.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: We implement FunSearch as a distributed system that has three types of workers: a programs database, samplers, and evaluators, which communicate asynchronously.
protocol_standardization.note: Proprietary internal components only; no standard agent/tool protocol mentioned.

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: an evolutionary procedure based on pairing a pre-trained LLM with a system-
loop_primitives.note: Closest value: an evolutionary loop in which the LLM samples programs, a systematic evaluator scores them, and the loop iterates. It could also be read as multi_attempt.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the LLM should instead be seen as a source of diverse (syntactically correct) programs with occasionally interesting ideas
planning_granularity.note: No planning step; LLM only emits candidate functions.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: a distributed system that has three types of workers: a programs database, samplers, and evaluators
multi_agent_topology.note: Only one LLM role (sampler); database and evaluators are non-LLM components, so this is closest to a fixed pipeline of specialised workers rather than multiple LLM agents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: samplers generate new functions using the pre-trained LLM, while evaluators assess programs
delegation_mechanism.note: No agent delegates to another agent.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: FunSearch suggests a solution, which is examined by researchers, who may note features of interest. These features are used to refine the search
human_in_loop.note: Human refinement is an offline research loop outside the automated run; no in-run gating.

short_term_state.evidence_quote: The programs database keeps a population of correct programs, which are then sampled to create prompts.
short_term_state.note: Island/cluster population database is the working state, not a conversation.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: The programs database stores the initial user-provided program, as well as all programs received from the evaluators.
long_term_memory.note: Persistent population of scored programs within an experiment; closest to episodic_db.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Every four hours, we discard all the programs from the m/2 islands whose best instances have the lowest score.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Programs generated by the LLM are evaluated and scored on a set of inputs.
self_verification.note: Harness-run evaluate function scores every candidate; incorrect programs are discarded.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: Programs that were incorrect (did not execute within the imposed time and memory limits, or produced invalid outputs) are discarded
retry_policy.note: Sampling continues indefinitely; failed candidates simply discarded and new ones sampled.

rollback.evidence_quote: Programs that are correct are sent to the programs database to be stored.
rollback.note: Nothing is mutated in place, so no rollback mechanism exists; island resets are population-level, not file reverts.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: the results in the paper are obtained using a total number of samples on the order of 10 6
termination_condition.note: Run ends after a sample budget / manual termination; 'This process is repeated until termination.'

cost_controls.evidence_quote: this keeps the overall cost and energy usage of experiments low
cost_controls.note: Cost reduced via cheap CPU evaluators and a fast-inference model, but no token budget, router or caching mechanism is described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: did not execute within the imposed time and memory limits
timeouts.note: Per-program execution time limit in the evaluator.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: a sandbox for safely executing generated code on our internal distributed system were used
execution_isolation.note: A sandbox is used; its exact nature (container/VM) is not specified.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: a sandbox for safely executing generated code on our internal distributed system were used
filesystem_access.note: Inferred from sandboxing; filesystem policy not described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: The samples from the LLM (i.e., the generated programs) are sent to the evaluators, which score programs by executing them on inputs of interest
permission_model.note: All generated programs are executed in the sandbox; no authorisation step.

tracing.evidence_quote: The programs database stores the initial user-provided program, as well as all programs received from the evaluators.
tracing.note: The program database with scores acts as the run record; no explicit tracing system described.

replayability.evidence_quote: Due to randomness in LLM sampling and in the evolutionary procedure, repeating an experiment can lead to different results.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: The input to FunSearch is a specification of the problem in the form of an evaluate function, which scores candidate solutions.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation is intrinsic to the harness; benchmark specs (bin packing, cap set) ship with the released code.

guardrails.evidence_quote: Programs that were incorrect (did not execute within the imposed time and memory limits, or produced invalid outputs) are discarded
guardrails.note: Sandboxed execution plus discarding invalid programs acts as the action policy.

target_domain.evidence_quote: the discovery of new scientific results for established open
target_domain.note: Built for mathematical and algorithmic discovery: cap sets and bin packing.

open_source.evidence_quote: a single-threaded implementation of the FunSearch pipeline are available as Python code in the Supplementary information and at https://github.com/google-deepmind/funsearch
open_source.note: Public repo; licence text not in evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we have empirically observed that the results obtained in this paper are not too sensitive to the exact choice of LLM, as long as it has been trained on a large enough corpus of code
model_agnostic.note: Codey and StarCoder both used; API access is sufficient.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: a single-threaded implementation of the FunSearch pipeline are available as Python code
primary_artifact.note: Only a single-threaded reference implementation accompanies the paper; coded from the paper.
